definition.name: annotate_native_function
definition.title: Annotate Native Function
definition.description: Atomically update one function name and/or entry comments, read them back, and return a refreshed complete function dossier. Ghidra changes its ephemeral session analysis database only; original executable bytes remain unchanged. Empty comment text clears that comment. Edits remain available to subsequent MCP calls until close; CLI returns the updated dossier before discarding its session. Invalid edits roll back the entire operation. Windows P0 and providers without this capability are unsupported.

name.description: Exact name used by this operation.

comment.description: Regular entry comment; empty text clears it

inline_comment.description: Inline entry comment; empty text clears it

__schema2.description: Regular entry comment; empty text clears it

__schema4.description: Inline entry comment; empty text clears it

stack_displacement.description: Observed signed stack byte displacement, encoded as decimal to preserve precision.

provider_value.description: Original provider display text, which may shorten the typed object.

decoding.description: When present, value retains native display text because typed bytes could not be decoded.

encoding_status.description: Whether the provider declares the encoding or REA infers it from the typed bytes and native display. This does not establish the original source's intended encoding.

swift_string_literals.description: Swift String literals decoded from constant register values. Absent when the provider does not decode them for this target.

swift_string_literal_omissions.description: Literal candidates omitted for capacity or unresolved control flow. Present exactly when swift_string_literals is present; empty when all examined use sites were classified.

end.description: Inclusive last address of this observed body range.

representation.description: The UTF-8 bytes are inside the two words.

address.description: A small literal has no storage of its own.

representation.description: An immortal literal whose words hold its count and a pointer to its bytes.

address.description: Address of a large literal's bytes.

__schema34.description: Instruction that consumes both words: a call, tail call, return, or paired store.

__schema35.description: Decoded UTF-8 text, including the canonical empty string.

__schema37.description: Observed constant register values, in register order.

address.description: Address of the literal's bytes.

__schema42.description: Why this candidate is omitted: capacity stopped decoding, or an unresolved jump left its use unknown.

availability_snapshot.remediation: Call open_binary with a supported local target.

definition.name: inspect_native_load_image
definition.title: Inspect Native Load Image
definition.description: Verify the provider's loaded DOS MZ or explicitly selected COM image against its immutable target snapshot: complete original/modified source-byte digests, header/module file mappings and memory digests, relocations and external entry. Returns measured observations and independent checks with mismatch coordinates. COM verification includes its imposed entry register context and does not claim PSP/runtime coverage. Overlay and uninitialized coverage remain explicit; other formats return unsupported. Does not execute or modify the target.

availability_snapshot.remediation: Call open_binary with a supported local target.

definition.name: inspect_native_data_type
definition.title: Inspect Native Data Type
definition.description: Inspect one recovered type by exact database category path or defined typed data address. Returns observed size, alignment, packing, fields, bitfields, enum values, and child type identities; source-level authority and flexible-tail semantics remain unknown unless substantiated.

document.description: Exact provider document or program identity.

availability_snapshot.remediation: Call open_binary with a supported local target.

definition.name: inspect_native_instruction
definition.title: Inspect Native Instruction
definition.description: Inspect one exact code or data address: decoded bytes, mnemonic, ordered operand tokens, flow, outgoing instruction references and typed incoming references where available. Incoming references preserve source, access kind, operand index and analysis provenance even at data addresses; they do not prove runtime access. Memory addressing decomposition is unavailable when the provider supplies only tokens. Data, interior instruction addresses and undecodable bytes are distinct outcomes.

document.description: Exact provider document or program identity.

mode.description: Provider-reported mode label. Per-address decoder context, when available, is reported separately; a program-wide label does not establish runtime encoding mode.

decoder_context.description: Observed per-address decoder context. Null means no value was available; omission means the provider or older capture does not expose this facet. The separate mode field retains the program language variant.

classification_evidence.description: Observed provider facts used to classify flow; older captures or other providers may omit them.

incoming_references.description: Static references to this exact code or data address, excluding synthetic entry-point references. An empty array means the provider examined the address and found none; null or omission means unavailable. Analyzer references do not prove literal addressing or runtime access.

primary.description: Provider primary-reference status, not proof of literal addressing or a runtime access. Null or omission means unavailable.

provenance.description: Provider subsystem reporting this reference; null or omission means unavailable.

source.description: Provider reference origin, such as analysis, default, imported or user_defined; null or omission means unavailable.

availability_snapshot.remediation: Call open_binary with a supported local target.

definition.name: resolve_native_call_targets
definition.title: Resolve Native Call Targets

Persistent GDB sessions are available only on Linux, where REA can verify live inferior output descriptors through /proc before detaching; macOS descriptor verification is not implemented, and Windows Job Object cleanup can terminate debugger inferiors. Optionally set inferior_tty to a caller-selected terminal for future inferior runs; REA verifies the setting through GDB/MI before the session becomes ready. The selected terminal must remain available after GDB exits. A live inferior can be detached during close only while this durable output sink remains verified. The session persists in this REA MCP server process and receives an explicit session ID.

inferior_tty.description: Caller-selected terminal path for future inferior runs. GDB must report the exact configured path before the session is ready.

__schema0.description: Caller-selected terminal path for future inferior runs. GDB must report the exact configured path before the session is ready.

definition.name: gdb_console
definition.title: Gdb Console
definition.description: Run one unrestricted GDB CLI command through MI interpreter-exec console and return raw MI, console, target, and log records inline with Evidence. A command timeout preserves collected records with completion_status unknown and stops the owned debugger session. Commands can execute shell, alter target state, access files, and use network. Closing the debugger never implies target termination. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

definition.name: close_gdb_session

definition.description: Close the owned GDB process after verifying the inferior state. REA never kills attached or remote targets as part of debugger cleanup. In a shared MCP server, this admitted close retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

definition.name: start_rizin_debug_session
definition.title: Start Rizin Debug Session
definition.description: Start a persistent Rizin debugger session using `-N` to suppress user settings and scripts while retaining plugins, `-0` for NUL framing, and `-d` with an optional caller-selected IO debugger backend. Requires a caller-selected Linux TTY for inferior stdout and stderr; the target may write directly to that terminal while running and after detach. REA verifies both destinations and `dbg.exitkills=false` before detaching. Backend and target capabilities depend on the installed build. The session lives in this REA MCP process. Persistent sessions require Linux `/proc` descriptor readback. In a shared MCP server, starting this session retires any active binary-analysis session; after target effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

definition.name: rizin_debug_command
definition.title: Rizin Debug Command
definition.description: Execute one unrestricted command in a persistent Rizin debugger session. Returns raw output inline with Evidence, including backend output interleaved before the completion marker. If the command exceeds the output or frame limit, `output_truncated` is true and `completion_status` is `unknown`; retained partial output is returned and the owned debugger session is stopped. Unsolicited frames already queued before the command make the session unavailable because correlation is ambiguous. Commands can access local files, shell, network, plugins, and target state; effects depend on the active backend and target. In a shared MCP server, this admitted command closes any active binary-analysis session; after its effects have settled, call open_binary before further analysis. Close an active Ghidra session explicitly first.

definition.name: inspect_analysis_view
definition.title: Inspect Analysis View
definition.description: Inspect selected views of completed binary-layout, JavaScript application, native analyze_function, inspect_artifact, inventory_artifact, inspect_wasm_artifact, inspect_macho, decode_interface_builder, inspect_evm_interface, inspect_managed_artifact, inspect_managed_members, inspect_android_package, inspect_dart_aot or inspect_web_network_capture Evidence without repeating analysis. Historical capture summaries return identity and counts without bodies or archive inventories. Capture views page retained records: view {kind: "capture", detail: "preview" | "complete", offset: 0, limit: 20}; preview selects recorded headline fields and binary descriptors, complete returns exact records with all sidecars. Offsets follow the selected parent record order, preserving original producer ordinals. Paging never reopens the source or reruns the decoder. For inspect_pcap_capture parents, kind pcap pages endpoints, dns-queries, tls-sni, protocols, http-uris or unattributed-addresses. Select an exact query for dns-addresses, or a tshark/capinfos stream for UTF-16 diagnostics text. Page totals count retained facts; source coverage remains explicit. Qlog summaries keep profile/scope and counts; kind qlog pages traces, streams, loss-declarations, incomplete-records, contributions, ranges or final-sizes. Except traces, select trace_index; stream-specific facets also require exact stream_id and direction. Facts retain all-recorded-events-before-selection scope, and interval overlap or endpoint loss declarations do not prove retransmission or network loss. The api-surface view groups retained HAR requests by method, origin and format-rule path template; templated segments are inferences. It reads no headers or bodies and reports no query values. For a retained record use source: {kind: "retained-evidence", evidence_id: "<parent_evidence_id>"}. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id from a summary receipt. Source kind is required. Portable source uses {kind: "inline", evidence: <complete Evidence>}. For layout, JavaScript, inventory, WASM, Mach-O, Interface Builder, EVM, managed artifact, Android package and Dart AOT sources, request a summary with view: {kind: "summary"}; summary is a view kind and has no facet. The WASM summary gives validation, counts, WAT digest/length, tool profile and execution/network states without reading WAT text. Select a layout mitigations/linkage facet, one section/symbol/module, or a stable page. Module pages include assets, bundled and source modules; use node_id for ambiguous or unavailable paths. Inventory uses view: {kind: "inventory", collection: "occurrences", logical_paths: ["package.json"], offset: 0, limit: 64}. Inventory views page nodes, occurrences, edges or integrity contradictions; occurrence logical_paths matches exact recorded strings (omitted means all available, [] means none). source_complete distinguishes complete inventories from partial source records; page exhaustion does not prove absence in a partial source. WASM views use kind wasm and facet sections/imports/exports/candidates/glue/wat/headers/details/tool_profile; text facets use UTF-16 code units and source forms remain exact. Mach-O views use kind macho and facet entrypoints/architectures/build_metadata/load_commands/dependencies/imports/exports/segments/provenance; source_exhaustive false means unreturned rows may exist. Interface Builder views use kind interface-builder and collection documents/nodes/edges/coverage; nodes and edges accept an exact document relative_path. EVM summary returns all inferred interface candidates, carrier/decoded identities and explicit unknowns without hex or duplicate stdout. EVM views use kind evm and facet functions/bytecode_hex/stdout/stderr; function pages preserve the original candidate rows, and text offsets/limits count UTF-16 code units (hex has two characters per decoded byte). Exhausting candidate pages does not establish global interface completeness. Managed artifact summaries preserve complete identity/classification, metadata status, module/MVID, frameworks, coverage and limitations without unrelated inventories. Managed pages use kind managed and collection references/resources/attributes, retaining source coverage and build-local token scope; page exhaustion does not establish complete metadata. Managed member summaries keep identity, selection with unmatched names, coverage and per-collection counts; managed-members pages use collection types/exported_types/fields/methods/member_refs/call_edges/field_accesses/user_strings and carry the source selection and coverage. Android package summaries retain all declarations, engine identity and counts without decoded manifest text. Android manifest pages use kind android, facet manifest, offset and limit in UTF-16 code units; source_status preserves partial decoded coverage even when the retained text page is exhausted. Dart AOT summary preserves target/ABI/library identity, snapshot headers and pool lower bounds. String pages use kind dart-aot, collection package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens; source coverage remains partial when the producer says partial. Native function Evidence requires kind native: view: {kind: "native", facet: "procedure"}. Facets select procedure, pseudocode, assembly, basic blocks, comments, callers/callees, references, unresolved calls, referenced strings/names, native API and high-pcode. Use nonnegative offset and a positive caller-selected limit (defaults 0 and 64); pseudocode uses UTF-16 code units, other native pages use rows. Returns artifact identity, parent Evidence ID, a distinct view digest, coverage, limitations and unknowns. Actual serialized size determines MCP transport admission; choose a smaller page or export the complete retained Evidence if needed.

definition.name: inspect_sqlite_database
definition.title: Inspect Sqlite Database
definition.description: Inspect an explicit local SQLite database snapshot and its existing sibling WAL without modifying source files or opening a native analysis provider. Requires Node.js 24.x >=24.15 or 26+ with native DatabaseSync.limits support, checked by the worker. Returns observed Evidence with database/WAL SHA-256 and a compact schema inventory. Selecting an exact ordinary table expands only its schema and samples rows (default 20, subject to byte and worker resource limits). Select exact columns in the requested order to avoid unrelated or large values; schema_scope=database explicitly expands the whole schema; returned rows retain 64-bit integers, text bytes and blobs with explicit truncation. No arbitrary SQL, view or virtual-table execution, extension loading, database repair, encryption support or live-snapshot atomicity claim. At most two inspections per provider are admitted; occupied capacity is retryable. An isolated temporary copy and owned worker enforce input, value/record, SQL-statement, JSON-reply, JavaScript-heap and deadline limits; overall native heap is not capped. Supply a quiescent snapshot for coherent database/WAL evidence.

definition.title: Inspect Web Network Capture
definition.description: Request detail summary for capture identity and counts; then page retained records with inspect_analysis_view kind capture (preview or complete), avoiding repeated decoding. SAZ preserves HTTP fields, XML metadata and encoded body/message bytes without replay or HAR conversion; encrypted archives are unsupported. Native mitmproxy requires caller-supplied mitmdump 12.2.3 on Linux. Browser transaction IDs, runtime attribution and original bytes of HAR Unicode text remain unknown.

definition.name: capture_process_scenario
definition.title: Capture Process Scenario
definition.description: Run one caller-selected command under a PTY and return process capture Evidence with residual unknowns. The renderer admits at most 1,000,000 combined terminal cells, computed as columns × (rows + scrollback); every resize uses the selected scrollback and must fit the same budget. Supply a smaller terminal shape when that product is too large; dimensions are never clamped. A command name resolves through the inherited PATH; the working directory defaults to the caller's current directory; host environment variables are inherited with scenario overrides. Environment keys cannot contain '=' or NUL, and REA_PROCESS_RUN_ID is reserved for process ownership. Filesystem snapshots are opt-in through filesystem_observation_paths. A positive finalization_ms makes a timeout or idle deadline send SIGTERM to the captured root through its start identity, keep observing, and send SIGKILL once after the interval; exit.finalization records each attempt with its delivery result and the observed exit, and cancellation still ends the run at once. The target runs with the current user's permissions; this is not a security sandbox.

action.title: Rewrite Action
action.description: The action performed when a rewrite rule matches. The exact fields used depend on the action type.

type.title: Action Type
type.description:
The rewrite action type index.
- Redirect(0): Redirect matching HTTP requests to a different URL.
- Replace Request(1): Replace the HTTP request path, headers and body with the preset values.
- Replace Response(2): Replace the HTTP response code, headers and body with the preset values.
- Modify Request(3): Dynamically modify HTTP request parameters, headers and body with matchers such as regular expressions.
- Modify Response(4): Dynamically modify HTTP response headers and body with matchers such as regular expressions.

redirectUrl.title: Redirect URL
redirectUrl.description: Used by Redirect(0) actions. The new URL to redirect to.

preserveHost.title: Preserve Host
preserveHost.description: Used by Redirect(0) actions. Whether to preserve the original Host header.

excludeUrl.title: Exclude URL Pattern
excludeUrl.description: Used by Redirect(0) actions. Matching URLs are excluded from redirect processing.

excludeWildcard.title: Use Wildcard Exclusion
excludeWildcard.description: Used by Redirect(0) actions. Whether excludeUrl should be treated as a wildcard pattern.

headers.title: Headers
headers.description: Used by Replace Request(1) and Replace Response(2) actions. A list of HTTP header key-value pairs.

items.title: String Entry
items.description: A key-value string entry, typically used for HTTP headers.

key.title: Key
key.description: The entry key, such as an HTTP header name.

value.title: Value
value.description: The entry value, such as an HTTP header value.

body.title: Rewrite Replace Body
body.description: A body payload used by replace HTTP request or replace HTTP response actions.

type.title: Body Type
type.description:
The body type index.
- None(0): No body.
- Text(1): A text body.
- Binary(2): A binary file body.

payload.title: Payload
payload.description:
The body content.
- None(0): Should be empty.
- Text(1): The text content of the body.
- Binary(2): The file path of the binary body content.

method.title: Replacement Request Method
method.description: Used by Replace Request(1) actions. The new request method to send.

path.title: Replacement Request Path
path.description: Used by Replace Request(1) actions. The new request path to send.

requestLineEnabled.title: Request Line Enabled
requestLineEnabled.description: Used by Replace Request(1) actions. Whether the request line rewrite is enabled.

code.title: Replacement Response Status Code
code.description: Used by Replace Response(2) actions. The new HTTP status code to return.

statusLineEnabled.title: Status Line Enabled
statusLineEnabled.description: Used by Replace Response(2) actions. Whether the status code rewrite is enabled.

headersEnabled.title: Headers Enabled
headersEnabled.description: Used by Replace Request(1) and Replace Response(2) actions. Whether header replacement is enabled.

bodyEnabled.title: Body Enabled
bodyEnabled.description: Used by Replace Request(1) and Replace Response(2) actions. Whether body replacement is enabled.

modifies.title: Modify Items
modifies.description: Used by Modify Request(3) and Modify Response(4) actions. The list of modify operations to apply.

id.title: Modify Item ID
id.description: The unique ID of the modify item.

type.title: Modify Type
type.description:
The modify type index.
- Modify Body(0): modify the request body.
- Add Query(1): add a query parameter.
- Modify Query(2): modify a query parameter.
- Remove Query(3): remove a query parameter.
- Add Header(4): add a header.
- Modify Header(5): modify a header.
- Remove Header(6): remove a header.

modify.title: Rewrite Modify Payload
modify.description: The modify payload for a single modify item. The exact structure depends on the `type` value.

pattern.title: Match Pattern
pattern.description: Used by Modify Body(0), Modify Query(2) and Modify Header(5) types. The pattern to match in the request body for modification.

replacement.title: Replacement
